<description>
Since #36895, `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` walks the items before the one it returns, so reading a whole witness stack through it is O(n^2).

This keeps a span for each item in `btck_WitnessStack`, which makes `btck_witness_stack_get_item_at` O(1) without changing its signature. `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` is O(n) instead of O(1), because it finds every item when it creates the witness stack.

Breaking changes:
- `btck_transaction_input_get_witness_stack` returns an owned `btck_WitnessStack*`, which must be destroyed with `btck_witness_stack_destroy`.
- The C++ wrapper's `WitnessStackView` is removed, and `GetWitnessStack()` returns a `WitnessStack`.
</description>
